title: split-kernel-bundles-and-add-adaptive-lazy-linking-for-gpu-runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over time the runtime container images have accumulated multiple monolithic kernel bundles (CUTLASS, Triton plugins, quantization kernels) that are linked and loaded eagerly at startup. This increases image size, probe time, and amplifies failure blast radius when a single kernel change requires a full image rebuild. Goal: Reduce cold-start probe latency and image size by splitting kernel bundles into smaller artifacts and implementing an adaptive lazy-linking loader that only materializes kernel shared objects on first use. This should preserve current ABI compatibility, support safe rollbacks, and improve iteration speed for kernel upgrades.

Scope: 1) Build and publish granular kernel bundle artifacts (cutlass-core, cutlass-quant, triton-plugins, misc-ops). 2) Implement a lazy-link loader in the runtime which performs deferred dlopen/dlsym with an exponential backoff and a small warmup cache. 3) Add feature flag to opt into lazy linking per deployment (hosted/dedicated/private). 4) Add CI validation to simulate partial bundle rollout and safe fallback to legacy monolith.

Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end startup probe time reduced by >=30% in mixed-model workloads (measured on p4dn-like instance profiles). - Runtime image size reduction >=12% for typical prod images. - No increase in P95 inference latency after warmup. - Rollback path validated: if a new bundle fails to load, fallback to the previous bundle within 30s without crashing serving processes. - Kernel upgrade docs and upgrade-playbook published.

Risks & trade-offs: - Increased complexity in artifact publishing and version mapping between bundles. Mitigation: unify artifact metadata and sign bundles. - Potential for first-request latency spike on cold worker when lazy-linking a hot kernel. Mitigation: warmup heuristics and prefetch lists for common models. - Compatibility with existing kernel probing logic. Mitigation: maintain legacy probe as a compatibility mode behind feature flag.

Implementation notes: - Artifact format: tarball with signed .so files and manifest.json (artifact metadata: bundle-version, symbols, ABI-hash). - Runtime: add kernel_loader component with APIs: ensure_bundle_loaded(bundle_id), probe_symbols(symbol_list), register_fallback(bundle_id). - CI: add stage that runs small end-to-end serving matrix with partial bundle presence. - Observability: emit metrics kernel_bundle.load.latency, kernel_bundle.load.failures, kernel_bundle.size.bytes and link to console dashboards.

Docs/Artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/Split+Kernel+Bundles+Spec  ; Drive design assets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KERNELSPLIT ; Design review notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GPUTRACE
comments: 2025-11-12 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after the ops postmortem highlighted slow probe times during cutlass rollout. Initial spike analysis attached to the Confluence doc.

2025-11-13 Marco Ruiz: Prototype of lazy-link loader sketched. Found that Triton plugin dlopen requires RTLD_GLOBAL for symbol resolution — prototype switches to symbolic manifest to avoid collisions. See prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823
2025-11-15 Review (SRE): Requested explicit fallback semantics and a health-check that marks worker unhealthy if bundle loading repeatedly fails for X attempts. Added to implementation notes.

2025-11-17 Marco Ruiz: Implemented bundle manifest parser and local cache. Integration tests added to simulate missing bundle and validated rollback path. CI job added: runtime-bundle-partial-rollout. Test run results: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/9876
2025-11-20 PM Review (Lena Chen): Prioritized for runtime-1.30. Please add a short migration guide for Dedicated customers (KMS signing checks) — assigned to Marco.

2025-11-20 Marco Ruiz: Addressed PM feedback and added KMS verification step for release process. Preparing final PR for feature-flag gating and metrics emission. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4899
